title: Training RNNs: Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT) 📚
description: Understand BPTT, gradient flow across time steps, and the issues that arise.

slides.title: Gradients Through Time 🕰️
slides.content:
# Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT)

The unrolled RNN is like a deep network with shared weights. To compute gradients:
1. Unroll the RNN over all time steps.
2. Apply standard backpropagation.
3. Accumulate gradients from each time step for the shared weights.

This is computationally expensive for long sequences.

slides.title: Vanishing & Exploding Gradients 🌊
slides.content:
# The Problem of Deep Networks

In a very deep network (many time steps), gradients can:
- **Vanish**: become extremely small → early time steps learn almost nothing.
- **Explode**: become enormous → unstable updates, NaN losses.

RNNs are especially prone because the same weights multiply over and over.

> Analogy: A game of telephone – the message gets distorted (vanishes) or amplified uncontrollably the longer the chain.

quizData.question: What causes vanishing gradients in RNNs?

options.text: Repeated multiplication of small weight matrices through many time steps

quizData.explanation: If the recurrent weight matrix has eigenvalues < 1, gradients shrink exponentially with time.

slides.title: Gradient Clipping 🚦
slides.content: A simple fix for exploding gradients: scale gradients if their norm exceeds a threshold.

slides.title: Truncated BPTT ✂️
slides.content:
# A Practical Solution

Instead of unrolling the full sequence (which might be thousands of steps), unroll only a fixed window (e.g., 100 steps). This speeds up training and limits gradient propagation length.

Keras automatically handles backpropagation over the entire sequence, but you can set `unroll=True` to speed up for shorter sequences.

slides.title: Don't Panic! 🛡️
slides.content: In practice, using LSTM or GRU largely mitigates vanishing gradients. They have special gating mechanisms that allow gradients to flow unchanged across many time steps.
